summary: Greenlee County, Arizona, tower on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest; its 1965 replacement is listed as standing and it reportedly survived the 2011 Wallow Fire.

facts.design: 54-foot K-brace steel tower with CL-100 cab and catwalk (1965 replacement)

events.note: Original 48-foot Aermotor tower, per the register's description; the Arizona history gives no date for the first tower
Register Built field gives 1965; the Arizona history says an earlier Aermotor model LX-25 was replaced by a 54-foot K-brace tower
Wallow Fire started a few days before a June 1, 2011 post placed it a couple of miles from the lookout; a June 2, 2011 post reported the tower safe after a burnout

evidence.supports: location on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest
original 48-foot Aermotor tower built in 1931, replaced by a 54-foot tower with CL-100 cab and catwalk
evidence.quote: The original 48' Aermotor tower with 7'x7' cab for Reno Lookout built on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest in 1931 has been replaced with a 54' tower and CL-100 cab with catwalk.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
earlier tower an Aermotor model LX-25; replaced in 1965 by a 54-foot K-brace steel tower
evidence.quote: 1965: An earlier Aermotor model LX-25 tower was replaced with a 54-foot high K-Brace steel tower with a CL-100 all steel cab.

evidence.supports: post dated June 1, 2011: fire started a few days earlier a couple of miles from the lookout (Wallow Fire)
evidence.quote: A fire started a few days ago just a couple miles from Reno Fire Lookout (the Wallow Fire) on the A-S National Forest (AZ).

evidence.supports: post dated June 2, 2011: tower safe after burnout around it
evidence.quote: The Reno Lookout is safe. A successful burnout operation was done around the tower.
Reno Greenlee 33.62086 -109.42917 Tower Standing NHLR US 830, AZ 77

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field (1965) matches the replacement tower. Its description dates the first tower to 1931. The Arizona history gives no date for the first tower.
The register calls the first tower a 48-foot Aermotor; the Arizona history calls it an Aermotor model LX-25 and gives no height. The two descriptions may fit the same tower.

notes_for_editor: Two web searches and the FFLA rentals check found no current visiting or rental listing, so the story says the sources do not say. The 1931 original comes only from the register's description. The 2011 fire fact rests on posts quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; no independent fire report was read. The FFLA list is undated, so standing status is as of an unknown date. The record's built 1965 is the replacement, so an editor may want to keep the 1931 and 1965 events as added here.
